scope: The B0 integration lane's checks of the five Phase-B branches (2026-09-27): the bits ParamJSONFile::load stores for 51 JSON number tokens on a floating-point, 64-bit integer, floating-point list and integer list parameter (tests/data/b0_release/json, json_release.tsv); FileHandler::loadExperiment's ParseError for an input whose name and content no type claims, through the seven ported tools that load with an allowed list; BaselineFilter with a DataPoints structuring element of a negative and of a fractional length below one.
method: ParamJSONFile.cpp, FileHandler.cpp, MorphologicalFilter.h and the tool sources read at the pins with git show. A driver (driver.cpp) built on the node with the Release install's compiler and libOpenMS's own core flags loads each JSON document of json_cases.tsv (written by make_inputs.py) and prints the stored doubles as their IEEE-754 bits; nine TOPP cases run the installed tools, each in a clean environment (env -i, per-case HOME, OPENMS_HOME_PATH and cwd, OPENMS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=ON, OPENMS_DATA_PATH pinned). Everything ran twice; the JSON records are identical, and the TOPP cases are identical once paths and run times are masked, except bf_dp_negative's standard error, which is the shell's report of the SIGSEGV and names a process id. run1 is retained under tests/data/b0_release and replayed by tests/param_json.rs (number_tokens_store_the_release_builds_bits) and tests/topp_b0_release.rs.
evidence_tier: oracle-generated (tier 1 executed differential) against the Release build; the documented differences (BaselineFilter refuses an element below one sample where the Release build completes or crashes; the lifecycle renders an Error::Parse inside 'parse error on line 0: ') are in docs/TOPP_CLI_SUPPORT.md.
